intro: Biggest rank disagreements between the SEI board and SP+, 2026 season: from the SP+ top 15 and from our own top 15.

teams.explanation: SP+ sits at #50 because the scoreboard says middle-class: +49 margin, #30 nationally, with a 23-29 loss at Indiana dragging the average. SEI reads the plays. The Wildcats' defense erases opposing pass games (early-down pass PPA allowed +2.53 SD, INT% +1.79) and the offense converts at an elite clip (points per drive +1.75, red-zone TD% +1.90) — the 34-13 win over Penn State is that profile talking. The cracks SP+ may be pricing: third-down run defense (-2.22) and penalties (-1.86).
hints: Process outran scoreboard: margin rank #30 (margin +49) but SEI #2.
SP+ halves: off #59, def #34.
Strongest metrics: Early pass PPA +2.53, RZ TD% +1.90, INT% +1.79.
Weakest metrics: 3rd rush PPA -2.22, Pen -1.86.

teams.explanation: SP+ pegs the offense at #84; SEI has it at #14. The 13-41 opening loss to Notre Dame anchors the scoreboard view (margin #31), but the play-level chart says the Badgers run the ball behind a line that wins the backfield: opponents stuffed at an elite rate behind them (Stuffed +2.78) while protecting the football (Fum% +2.28). The defense sits near-average in SP+'s eyes (#19) and ours (#15). Discipline is the one ugly column: penalty rate -2.75.
hints: Process outran scoreboard: margin rank #31 (margin +48) but SEI #7.
SP+ halves: off #84, def #19.
Strongest metrics: Stuffed +2.78, Fum% +2.28, Early pass PPA +2.09.
Weakest metrics: Pen -2.75, Stuff -2.32.

teams.explanation: 5-0 and +70 keeps SP+ at #11, but the plays say the wins were closer than the record: Houston by 2, Oregon State by 11. Our offense half sits at #54 — the Red Raiders move the ball at a league-average pace, and the margin is carried by takeaways (INT% +2.38) rather than efficiency. No offensive metric clears the bar. When the one-possession games bounce the other way, this profile is a .500 profile.
hints: Scoreboard outran process: margin rank #17 (margin +70) but SEI #30.
Offense drives the gap: SEI off #54 vs def #20.
SP+ halves: off #11, def #17.
Strongest metrics: INT% +2.38, Early rush PPA +1.51.

teams.explanation: SP+'s #25 tracks the +48 margin and the 24-31 loss at Mississippi State. SEI is at #10 because the Tigers win the run game on both sides: early-down PPA against opposing rushes (+1.94) and third-down run defense (+1.74), with points per drive allowed (+1.60) rounding out a top-15 defense. The 45-17 shellacking of Florida is the profile talking; Oxford was where it wasn't.
hints: Process outran scoreboard: margin rank #31 (margin +48) but SEI #10.
SP+ halves: off #40, def #14.
Strongest metrics: Early rush PPA +1.94, 3rd rush PPA +1.74, Early pass PPA +1.64.

teams.explanation: The only real argument on this list. SP+ has Georgia #1 overall and #1 on both halves; the +130 margin backs it. SEI's offense half agrees (#5: third-down pass PPA +2.43, points per drive +1.86) but the defense half sits at #39 — the Bulldogs have rarely forced anything behind the line of scrimmage (opponents stuffed -1.71) while Arkansas moved to 17 and Vanderbilt to 14. A margin model cannot see an untested defense; an efficiency model can only measure what was tested.
hints: Defense drives the gap: SEI off #5 vs def #39.
SP+ halves: off #1, def #1.
Strongest metrics: 3rd pass PPA +2.43, Pts/drive +1.86.
Weakest metrics: Stuff -1.71.

teams.explanation: SP+ loves the offense (#5); we rank the defense #35 and that plus the schedule is most of the gap. The Ducks' margin is +13 (#56) after the 31-39 loss at Oklahoma State, and their penalty rate is -2.20 — the worst discipline on the board. What is real: third-down pass PPA +2.80 says Oregon wins the obvious downs. What is not: preventing anything between them, where the mirror features sit near average.
hints: Process outran scoreboard: margin rank #56 (margin +13) but SEI #16.
Defense drives the gap: SEI off #15 vs def #35.
SP+ halves: off #5, def #25.
Strongest metrics: 3rd pass PPA +2.80, INT% +1.82, Pen yd +1.71.
Weakest metrics: Pen -2.20.

teams.explanation: The split is the line of scrimmage. Our defense half is #6 — sack rate +1.96, red-zone touchdown defense +1.71, allowed explosiveness +1.59 — while the offense sits at #55, dragged down by getting sacked at a bad clip (sack rate taken -1.81). SP+'s #14 splits the difference. The 17-20 loss to Texas was the profile's offense problem showing: one score short all afternoon.
hints: Offense drives the gap: SEI off #55 vs def #6.
SP+ halves: off #14, def #26.
Strongest metrics: Sack% +1.96, RZ TD% +1.71, Exp +1.59.
Weakest metrics: Sack% -1.81.

teams.explanation: The defense is the board-seller: sack rate +3.31 SD — off the chart — early-down pass PPA allowed +3.01, havoc +2.87, points per drive allowed +1.73. That rush put 51 on Clemson and held Texas A&M to 6. SP+ sits at #10 because the offense's #22 half and the 24-32 loss at Ole Miss pull it down. We weight what the pass rush does to opposing drives more than one bad Saturday in Oxford.
hints: SP+ halves: off #22, def #4.
Strongest metrics: Sack% +3.31, Early pass PPA +3.01, Havoc +2.87.
